provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — exploitation of CVE-2018-13379 is detectable at the appliance/WAF via requests to the vulnerable /remote/fgt_lang?lang= sslvpn path-traversal endpoint, FortiOS access logs, and version/patch-state monitoring of exposed Fortinet devices

medium — anomalous VPN authentication (new geolocation/ASN, impossible travel, off-hours logon, reused leaked credentials) is detectable via VPN/identity authentication analytics, but blends with legitimate remote access

medium — reuse of valid/leaked credentials is detectable via authentication-anomaly analytics and leaked-credential monitoring, but individual valid logons are inherently hard to distinguish from legitimate use
high — PowerShell script-block/module logging captures the implants' web requests to cloud APIs and command execution; suspicious PowerShell making OneDrive/Dropbox Graph API calls is a strong signal

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — cmd.exe spawned as a child of an unusual .NET/C++ implant process, with command output redirected, is detectable via process-lineage telemetry, but cmd.exe use is common and needs parent-process context

medium — loading of unsigned/unusual named DLLs from user-writable paths by an implant process is detectable via image-load (Sysmon EID 7) telemetry, but requires baselining of legitimate module loads
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational); tasks pointing at implant binaries in user-writable or masqueraded paths are a solid detection when baselined

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation of .lnk files in Startup folders pointing at implant binaries is detectable via file-creation monitoring of Startup paths (Event ID 4663 / Sysmon EID 11)
high — InstallUtil.exe invoking a non-standard assembly (especially from a user-writable path, with uninstall/install verbs) is a rare, high-fidelity command-line detection

medium — deletion of recently created implant/staging files is detectable via file-deletion auditing (Sysmon EID 23/26) correlated with prior write events, but file deletion is common and needs context

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — binaries with legitimate-looking names but wrong signer/path/hash (e.g., 'Microsoft Malware Protection.exe' unsigned, DropBox.exe not from Dropbox) are detectable via signature-vs-name and path baselining

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — heavily obfuscated .NET assemblies (obfuscator artifacts, high-entropy resources) are detectable via static/entropy analytics and obfuscator-specific YARA, but require dedicated scanning

medium — keylogger modules register low-level keyboard hooks / GetAsyncKeyState polling and write a growing keystroke-log file; detectable via API-hook heuristics, EDR behavioral signatures and log-file creation, but requires endpoint depth

medium — screenshot utilities generate periodic image files and call screen-capture APIs; detectable via file-creation patterns and EDR behavioral detection, though not as crisp as a discrete log event
medium — access to camera/DirectShow devices by an unusual process and the AForge.NET dependency are detectable via device-access and image-load telemetry, but require targeted endpoint visibility

medium — HTTP beacons carrying Base64-encoded username/IP to IP-only C2 on non-standard ports are detectable via proxy/NetFlow analytics and URI-pattern signatures, but HTTP C2 blends with normal web traffic without the specific indicators

detection_candidates.technique_name: Application Layer Protocol: File Transfer Protocols
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — outbound FTP from workstations to IP-only external servers on non-standard ports (2121) is unusual and detectable via NetFlow/proxy and FTP-protocol logging

medium — cloud C2 blends with legitimate OneDrive/Dropbox/Mega traffic, but is detectable via a non-browser/PowerShell process making Graph/Dropbox/Mega API calls, anomalous OAuth-app consents in the tenant, and read/write of tasking files (data.txt/cd.txt/response.json); needs cloud + endpoint correlation
medium — Base64-encoded username/IP tokens in HTTP request URIs are a distinctive pattern detectable via proxy/URI content inspection, but require signature tuning to avoid legitimate Base64 traffic
medium — raw TCP sessions from workstations to IP-only C2 on unusual ports (1302) are detectable via NetFlow/connection analytics as non-standard, unrecognized-protocol egress
medium — outbound connections on uncommon high ports (63047, 5055, 1302) to external IP-only hosts are detectable via NetFlow/firewall analytics as anomalous egress

high — Plink execution with tunneling/port-forward command-line arguments and outbound SSH from non-admin workstations to external IP-only servers are detectable via process command-line and network telemetry

medium — implant processes writing new executable/DLL modules to disk shortly after cloud/C2 fetches are detectable via process+file-write correlation, but blend with legitimate downloads without the process context

medium — outbound data volume anomalies over the same non-standard-port C2 sessions are detectable via NetFlow/egress analytics, but distinguishing exfil bytes from beacon traffic requires volumetric baselining

detection_candidates.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — uploads to OneDrive/Dropbox/Mega by a non-browser/implant process, and large data movement to newly consented OAuth apps, are detectable via cloud audit logs, CASB/DLP and endpoint process correlation, but legitimate cloud sync creates noise

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — access arriving through a trusted service-provider connection is largely off the victim's own endpoint telemetry; hunt candidate via review of third-party/managed-service access, unusual provider-originated sessions, and inter-organization trust monitoring
low — in-house malware development happens off-victim; the resulting implants are where detection lands. Intel/hunt candidate for tracking new Creepy-family variants
low — acquisition of public code/libraries is off-victim; downstream execution of the resulting modules is the detection surface. Intel/hunt candidate
low — tool acquisition itself is off-endpoint; downstream Plink/AirVPN use is where detection lands. Intel/hunt candidate
low — adversary VPS acquisition is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via infrastructure tracking (HostGW ranges, IP-only C2 clusters)

low — creation of attacker-controlled cloud apps/accounts is off-victim; the on-host cloud C2 and tenant-side OAuth-app grants are the detection surface. Intel/hunt candidate (enterprises can hunt anomalous OAuth application consents)
low — in-memory decoding leaves little discrete signal; hunt candidate via behavioral/memory analysis rather than a crisp log event
low — file/directory enumeration by an implant is common and noisy; meaningful only within a tight process-lineage/recon-burst window. Hunt candidate
low — process enumeration is ubiquitous and low-signal; hunt candidate via correlation with other implant behavior
low — host information gathering is common; the distinguishing signal is the encoded exfil in the beacon rather than the discovery itself. Hunt candidate
low — reading local network configuration is common admin/implant behavior; hunt candidate correlated with encoded C2 beacons
low — querying the current user is trivial and ubiquitous; hunt candidate only in combination with the encoded-beacon pattern
low — clipboard access is a common API with heavy legitimate use; poor discrete signal, hunt candidate via behavioral correlation
low — local file collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging/archiving patterns and process-lineage context. Hunt candidate

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Library
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — in-process ZIP creation via a library leaves little discrete telemetry (no external archiver process); hunt candidate via file-write of archive files preceding egress
low — AES-encrypted C2 payloads are opaque on the wire; detection relies on the host process and the Mega-service destination rather than content. Hunt candidate
low — VPN/proxy egress blends with legitimate traffic and is largely visible only as connections to known VPN endpoints; hunt/intel candidate via VPN-exit IP reputation
